notes.title: Dystopian Detectives Double Feature – Available Now!
notes.content:
Investigators,

We are pleased to announce a new initiative in collaboration with the brilliant minds behind Cyber Manhunt 2: New World. Introducing the Dystopian Detectives Double Feature Bundle, an exclusive offering designed to enhance your investigative expertise. [b]Take advantage of a 15% discount on this unique bundle today.[/b]

This package includes groundbreaking software to enhance your investigative skills within [strike]dystopian[/strike] stable and prosperous environments. Engage in intricate narratives and rigorous investigative tasks, offering hours of immersive and intellectually stimulating scenarios to hone your expertise.

[h3]Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25928706/beea85a8a3ac4b8743e16f32581f1b249745db50.png[/img]
Big Brother has arrived - and it’s you. Investigate the lives of citizens to find those responsible for a series of terror attacks. Information from the internet, personal communications, and private files are all accessible to you. But, be warned, the information you supply will have consequences.

[i]“Grabs the problem of how we balance our own liberty and our safety and turns it into a thrilling adventure.”[/i]
[i]9/10 – Polygon[/i]

[h3]Cyber Manhunt 2: New World[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25928706/959c807194952eb58ea6400f7487169d03b3e44c.png[/img]
Discover a digital realm shrouded in mystery in Cyber Manhunt 2: New World. Sequel to the award-winning narrative puzzle game. Play as an AI assistant in a major corporation. Deploy intricate social engineering tactics and expose hidden truths in a world of ambition and high-tech deception.

[i]“This game is wild, frankly, it's crazy wild”[/i]
[i]Pirate Software[/i]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/43083/Dystopian_Detectives_Double_Feature/]To the bundle[/url]

Seize this opportunity to refine your investigative acumen. Purchase the bundle today and immerse yourself in this unparalleled double feature experience.

notes.title: New languages: Italian, Japanese and Indonesian
notes.content:
Investigators,

With the help of our loyal community of international agents we were finally able to make the Orwell system available in three more languages: From today you will be able to utilize Orwell in [b]Italian, Japanese, as well as Indonesian[/b]. You are hereby [b]encouraged[/b] to appreciate their effort.

As always, you can find detailed update instructions below.


Stay vigilant
The Orwell administration


[h1]Patchnotes Version 1.4.7424[/h1]
[h2]Content[/h2]
[list][*]added community localizations for Italian, Japanese and Indonesian[/list]
[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list][*]fixed a bug where the Insider tool wasn't unlocked correctly in Episode 3 on an OS with Turkish language setting[/list]

notes.title: The Localizations Update is here!
notes.content:
Investigators,

We are constantly scouting for new recruits for the Orwell Project. But, as many of you have legtimately voiced, our surveillance effort would never be able not realize its full potential as long as it didn't include more languages.

This changes today! The Government of The Nation has spared no expense to present you official localizations of the Orwell software in
[list]
[*]German
[*]French
[*]Spanish
[*]Russian
[*]Chinese
[/list]
as well as an unofficial localization in Portuguese (Brazil), put together by some of our most loyal citizens on translate.orwell-game.com. Also, we would like to say thank you to all our citizens who have pointed out [strike]errors[/strike] minor imperfections in the Public Localization Beta, which is hereby concluded. Note that more languages will be added through future updates.

Additionally, the update brings tons improvements our engineers have worked on tirelessly in the recent months, such as a much demanded [b]phone call text speed slider[/b], a [b]brand new [strike]hack effect[/strike] intrusion warning[/b], some [b]reworked documents[/b], and [b]much shorter loading times[/b].

Please refer to the full changelog below for a detailled list of improvements and additions.


As always, remain vigilant.
The Orwell Project Administration


[h1]Changelog Version 1.3[/h1]

[b]Content and feature changes[/b]
[list][*]added official localizations for German, French, Spanish, Russian, Simplified Chinese (change language from settings menu)
[*]added community localization for Portuguese (Brazil) [THANKS TO OUR COMMUNITY ON TRANSLATE.ORWELL-GAME.COM!!]
[*]added a slider for text speed in phone calls
[*]slightly reworked timing of events such as comments by Symes
[*]all documents now dynamically adapt to content
[*]completely reworked the layout of some websites
[*]completely reworked some pictures
[*]slightly changed writing in places
[*]Spoiler episodes 2 & 5: [spoiler]completely reworked the hacking/glitch effect on Thought and in the Orwell system[/spoiler]
[*]Spoiler episodes 5: [spoiler]the ending sequence now features a dark overlay to make it clearer what can be clicked and what cannot[/spoiler][/list]

[b]Technical improvements[/b]
[list][*]greatly reduced loading times for savegames
[*]reduced memory footprint
[*]improved document loading, now loads contents element by element[/list]

[b]Bugfixes[/b]
[list][*]phone calls will now correctly maintain their vertical scroll position if the call is still running
[*]overlays no longer freeze after uploading a Datachunk
[*]fixed a sound bug when music was muted during the closing cutscene
[*]fixed tons of typos in the English original text[/list]

notes.title: The Public Localization Beta has started!
notes.content:
Investigators,

We’re stoked to invite you to the [b]Public Beta of the localizations of Orwell: Keeping an Eye on You[/b]! These last months we put a ton of work into the project and it has proven to be much more effort than we thought initially thought: To make it happen, we had to rebuild large portions of the game from the ground up. Thank you so much for your patience sending positive feedback our way! :)

Since a lot of rework comes with many things that might go wrong, we’d like to put the current game state to a public test, for which we need [b]YOU[/b]. As you know, many vigilant eyes will spot much more than only a few!

For instructions how to join please read on.

[h1]Languages included[/h1]
This public beta includes the following languages:
[list]
[*]German (Deutsch)
[*]Spain (Español)
[*]French (Français)
[*]Russian (Русский)
[*]Simplified Chinese (简体中文)
[/list]
Languages from the public translation project at translate.orwell-game.com will be added in later updates (by the way, you can still help bring Orwell to your language there!).

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25928706/4b6e614e1ada3e7e7f48d28b2cdf84c6e2b646c9.gif[/img]

[h1]How to join the Beta[/h1]
[b]Whoa, easy now: If you never played Orwell before, you definitely should wait for the final public release of the localizations for the best experience. The final release shouldn’t be too far off now.[/b]

Moving forward, you’ll have access to a fully playable [b]IN-DEVELOPMENT BUILD[/b], which means:
[list]
[*][b]YOUR EXISTING SAVEGAMES (PROFILES) MAY BECOME CORRUPTED!![/b] Please make backup copies of those (look for them in Documents\My Games\Orwell folder). We do not kid.
[*]There are unfinished, not proofread, and missing translations.
[*]There may be bugs and technical issues preventing game progress, possibly permanently.
[/list]
Note that we can’t provide support for the Beta or repair broken savegames from it.

You can find a list of known issues here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1CdVXT1mZ8so2w8NsgmThCgRowO0BgZ5aidAf8BMNGYY/edit?usp=sharing

To access the beta build, open up your Steam library and find Orwell. Right click it and select “Properties…”, then “Betas”. Enter the password ‘PublicLocaBeta’ (without ‘’) and confirm by clicking “Check Code”. There should now be a new option in the dropdown menu above named “public_localization_beta”. Select that, then wait for Steam to finish updating Orwell.

Done! Fertig! Et voilà ! You now have access to the Beta!

[h1]Reporting issues[/h1]
It’d be great if you could report issues while you’re at it! Please go to the following Google form to report them: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdZrT1ViBYmS9Ujdty78EJE4VNFSU8sCyvA-spv_N-ubgUSwg/viewform

Thanks for helping to make our game better! :)

Remain vigilant!
Vanessa, Michael and Daniel from Osmotic Studios

notes.title: BLOG POST: Orwell was released... and the world changed
notes.content:
[url=http://www.surpriseattackgames.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/Orwell_Ignorance_Screenshot1.jpg][img]http://www.surpriseattackgames.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/Orwell_Ignorance_Screenshot1-1024x576.jpg[/img][/url]

[b]In the first of a series of blog posts on Orwell: Ignorance is Strength, Osmotic Studios takes a look at how things have changed since the release of Orwell: Keeping an Eye on You, and the impact of those changes on the game, their studio, and the world.[/b]

- - -


On October 20, 2016, we released Orwell. After almost three years of development, and an unswerving belief in a game concept that had always been perceived as risky, our ‘baby’ was out the door, released as five weekly episodes. But, risky or not, from day one, we knew we had succeeded, attracting players who were looking for a new gaming experience, with a story to match.

A lot has happened since the release of Orwell. We’ve continually received many positive responses from both players and game critics, which has been wonderful. Especially since we felt like we’d been carrying around a huge responsibility: we were not only trying to entertain players, but also spark thoughts about highly topical issues that people may agree or disagree with. We always made a point about not wanting to impose opinions on people but instead give them the freedom to choose their side. Creating a gaming system where this was possible was certainly not easy. So, the messages we got from players about how Orwell had moved them emotionally (no matter which side they were on) were perhaps what fulfilled us most after the release of Season One.

But things not only changed for us as a studio; the world changed, too. The original inspiration for Orwell were the Snowden revelations, leaking facts about how the US government is collecting personal online data on a huge scale. In late 2016 through to early 2017, the US election campaign showed us that social media and the internet in general is not only an important tool to gain data, but also one of the most important forces to drive public opinion.

With that in mind, we felt that since Orwell: Keeping an Eye on You shows how powerful your online data can be, within an investigative context, it’s a logical next step to address what could be done with this data aside from deciding who is innocent or guilty. What if, as a player, you were able to reuse it and even spread new ideas through it? The discussion about fake news, alternative facts and the power of media manipulation inspired this and was the reason why we came up with the first concept for Orwell: Ignorance is Strength.

The central theme of Ignorance is Strength is the power of influence over the masses and the fight over this power. Compared to Season One, Season Two is more an open confrontation over this fight over influence and less about uncovering things. It asks the question, ‘How far can the power of fabricating stories and spreading them via the internet be used as a weapon?’. And, further, whether the ends justify the means. In addition, it questions truth itself and shows how easily it can be bent towards a certain direction, especially in the current digital information age.

[url=http://www.surpriseattackgames.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/Orwell_Ignorance_Screenshot3.jpg][img]http://www.surpriseattackgames.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/Orwell_Ignorance_Screenshot3-1024x576.jpg[/img][/url]

Early screenshot of Orwell: Ignorance is Strength.


The story revolves mainly around the character Raban Vhart, who is an immigrant of the Nation's neighbouring country Parges. He owns a blog called The People's Voice that is very anti-government and also criticizes the Pargesian president. Raban does not hesitate to bend the truth towards his own opinion and his main goal is to free his beloved home land from the establishment that caused civil unrest and even war in the shattered country.

The player is once again recruited by the government in order to let justice prevail and ensure the stability of The Nation. After passing an aptitude test, they join ‘The Office’, a top secret government agency within Orwell. The player's job is to fight back against Raban, using the government's own ways of influencing the masses.

Since the player is part of a more secretive government agency than in Season One, they also have more extensive tools that not only allow them to submit information to the profiler, but also reuse this information to search websites, enter passwords, break into a wider range of digital devices, and more. We made these changes because players would then have options for interaction and it fit perfectly into the general concept as well. These additional options make the gameplay a bit more complex, but since our basic game mechanic is rather minimalist, we felt it would be great to build on this and increase the challenge.

Orwell: Ignorance is Strength is set chronologically parallel with events in the first game. Players who have experienced Keeping an Eye On You will know that its story is self-contained and pretty much comes full circle. It would have felt artificial to simply attach a new storyline to that. Additionally, the game had a few quite different outcomes at its end. If we had wanted to continue from there we would have needed to declare one of the specific endings canon, which we felt would have undermined the players’ previous choices. The choice to make the new story play out simultaneously with the previous one opens up the very interesting possibility to give some of the old choices new meanings from a different perspective, while at the same time giving background to some of the events in Parges that were only briefly mentioned in the previous game.

Once again, with Ignorance is Strength, we hope to spark thoughts and move players emotionally. Perhaps it will even make players more sensitive in terms of how they look at the authenticity of online news and data in general. But we still do not want to tell players what to think.

The game is certainly a reflection on what is currently going on in the world and how the tensions of public debates are increasing. Ignorance is Strength has a generally darker tone , which is more confrontational and more intense. The characters all have their own battles to fight with themselves as well. We hope that players will be able to reflect on the central themes outside of the real world and dwell on these ideas.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bbrsck9Ag2I

notes.title: Update to Version 1.2 (Changelog)
notes.content:
Investigators,

as you may know, over the recent months we have been very busy working on season two of Orwell, Orwell: Ignorance is Strength, which you can wishlist here:

http://store.steampowered.com/app/633060/Orwell_Ignorance_is_Strength/

During the development we have solved a lot of issues with the game's technical base which we also want to apply to the original Orwell game. We're releasing these improvements with Orwell 1.2 today!

Most notably we increased the game's performance in terms of image loading times and memory usage, but also fixed a nasty bug that sometimes caused already discovered conflicted datachunks to be displayed as not being discovered, causing some confusion (this mainly occurred during Episode 2). 

Note: Your saved profiles are NOT backwards compatible, which means a 1.2 profile won't necessarily load on a version 1.1 game client. Please update the game on any devices to version 1.2 to avoid running into this issue.

As always you can find the full changelog below.


Stay vigilant,
the Osmotic Studios team


[h1]Changelog Version 1.2[/h1]

[b]Content Changes[/b]
[list]
[*]added a wishlist screen for Orwell: Ignorance is Strength when quitting the game; this can be disabled in said screen
[*]fixed a variety of inconsistencies in expressions (like "government"/"Government")
[*]fixed a variety of typos
[*]SPOILER EPISODE 1: [SPOILER]changed an adviser commentary in regard to Cassandra being depressive that could be out of context if the player didn't add a datachunk on her attitude before[/SPOILER]
[*]SPOILER EPISODE 2: [SPOILER]prevented that the player could solve the objective on Abraham's profession before having added the datachunk on his students and the number of protests, which would then result in a logical inconsistency[/SPOILER]
[*]SPOILER EPISODE 3: [SPOILER]fixed wrong titles of various people on the defaced Party people website[/SPOILER]
[*]SPOILER EPISODE 5: [SPOILER]added a new commentary in which Catherine warns the player when opening her PC's desktop that further investigating her will have consequences[/SPOILER]
[*]SPOILER EPISODE 5: [SPOILER]harrison.txt will now be displayed on initiate's PC in Episode 5 (it had never been visible before)[/SPOILER]
[*]SPOILER EPISODE 5: [SPOILER]Catherine will now comment every datachunk the player uploads on himself/herself (provided she didn't switch off her PC before)[/SPOILER]
[*]SPOILER EPISODE 5: [SPOILER]Catherine will no longer comment on anything after she switches off her PC[/SPOILER][/list]

[b]Technical Fixes[/b]
[list][*]decreased overall memory usage
[*]improved overall performance and loading times
[*]implemented a skip label to the intro cut scene being displayed when the player presses any key
[*]main menu logo animation now plays more fluidly
[*]added a loading cursor while booting up the game
[*]added a warning if a savegame originates from a newer version than the current client; this only works for future versions of the game though
[*]added different layouts of lines underneath tool icons that get switched according to the currently opened tool
[*]category buttons in the Profiler where there aren't any updates are now disabled
[*]mails can now be scrolled correctly if their content exceeds the Listener window
[*]fixed a bug where the game started with a big cursor for a brief moment on some platforms
[*]fixed a bug where the breadcrumb navigation (Insider) didn't show the whole document path after loading savegames multiple times
[*]fixed a bug that prevented already discovered conflicted datachunks to be shown as discovered in the datachunk information window of their counterparts if those datachunks were on a website that was updated several times (this could occur mainly on the Thought website in Episode 2)
[*]fixed a bug that some characters had their names displayed as "Unknown Person" in the corresponding Listener bookmarks when they were actually known
[*]fixed a bug of wrong spacing between insider bookmarks
[*]fixed a bug that led to too much space at the bottom of some websites
[*]fixed an issue where a text box or image outline of a chunk was highlighted on hover, before hovering the actual chunk itself (the box is always a bit larger than the chunk)
[*]fixed a bug where images on Insider devices were not displayed correctly when opening documents for the first time
[*]fixed a savegame bug which could occur when the day was completed while an adviser commentary was still waiting to be displayed
[*]fixed a bug that sometimes led to datachunk boxes not fitting their text in Listener calls after loading a savegame
[*]SPOILER EPISODE 5: [SPOILER]fixed a bug where the number of remaining datachunk uploads weren't correct when loading a savegame at a certain point in the game[/SPOILER]
[*]SPOILER EPISODE 5: [SPOILER]fixed a bug where the "uploads remaining" label was displayed after loading a game even though there weren't any uploads left[/SPOILER]
[*]SPOILER EPISODE 5: [SPOILER]fixed a display bug of the datachunks on the Player Evaluation website[/SPOILER][/list]

[b]Known Issues[/b]
[list][*]savegames are NOT backwards compatible (1.2 savegames do not run on 1.1 or lower clients); there are no warnings being displayed in version 1.1 or lower
[*]Linux: blur shaders have been disabled throughout the game[/list]

notes.title: The Rewind Update, IGF, GDC & PAX East!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25928706/1e638892fcf6248aeaed178c4c19e0529349f9e4.png[/img]
Hello investigators,

Today we are excited to release a brand new update for Orwell, an update that introduces one of the most requested features we've had from you all!

The Rewind Update will allow all players who have completed the game to "rewind" their save to the beginning of any chosen day, erasing all choices and allowing them to continue and explore other paths. Want to see how things pan out in day three if you made some other choices? Simply select day 3 from the menu and it's almost as if Symes has accidentally deleted all the Datachunks you submitted in days three, four and five!

To access the Episode Selection feature, you will need to access the Profile Options area. The Episode selection button will be locked until you have completed the game at least once, however after completion, it will be available for all new and existing profiles. Any unlocked episode is colored while the rest is grayed out. Click on the episode you want to revert your progress to, then click "Load Episode" and confirm.

Be aware that loading a previous episode [b]PERMANENTLY[/b] reverts your progress to the beginning of that episode. This cannot be undone, so make sure you are willing to revert your save before doing so!

We know that the update has taken quite some time. Messing around with save games is never an easy task for developers, so the team at Osmotic has been taking their time to ensure it is done correctly. Initial testing shows that everything is operational, however they may be some fringe cases with some problems. Please report those cases in the Steam forums, so we can make sure that they don't slip through the cracks.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25928706/ddb310b9f2e53e7e78958b969c8ce6abf99f31e8.png[/img]

In other news, Osmotic and Surprise Attack Games will be attending GDC 2017, where Osmotic will be hosting an Orwell booth in the IGF Finalist area. We are honoured to be up for the Excellence in Narrative Award, and we can't wait to meet all the devs that will be attending! If you are going to the show, make sure you stop on by and meet the team!

During next week, DRM-free fans can pick up a copy of Orwell on on other stores! The build will be on parity with the Steam build, so if you have some friends who want to hide from the prying eyes of DRM, make sure you let them know.

Finally, Surprise Attack Games will be heading along to PAX East, and will be showcasing Orwell alongside their other titles. You can find them in the PAX Aus Roadshow area, marked clearly in the show guide, and a giant sign above the booth on the show floor. Make sure you head along and show your support if you're making it out to Boston this year!

notes.title: Orwell nominated at SXSW and update to Version 1.0.6236
notes.content:
Investigators,

Orwell is nominated for the Matthew Crump Cultural Innovation Award at SXSW 2017 alongside That Dragon, Cancer and 1979 Revolution: Black Friday and others, which is a big honor for us! Thanks so much for making this possible!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25928706/6c06a626fe5db4bccafba0e77a3c69deed57c50b.png[/img]

Also we have just updated the game to Version 1.0.6236 across all platforms, which is mainly intended to add free window resizing and fix various crashes and instabilities. You can find patchnotes below.

Please note that this patch doesn't include the Episode Selection feature yet. The feature will most likely be released with a February update.

Stay vigilant!
Your Osmotic Studios Team


[h1]Patchnotes Version 1.0.6236[/h1]

[b]Content Fixes[/b]
[list][*]Catherine no longer shows up as "Unknown person" in the Profiler.
[*]Added an additional datachunk to clarify who the "Unknown person" related to Josef Langley is.
[*]Fixed some typos.[/list]

[b]Technical Fixes[/b]
[list][*]The game window can now be resized freely in windowed mode.
[*]Fixed various startup crashes.
[*]Fixed a crash that could occur right after 100% of savegame loading.
[*]Fixed various stalls (that also could crash the application) while loading or playing.
[*]Fixed brief CPU stall when starting to load a profile, just before the loading circle switches to the grey 0% state.
[*]Fixed a bug that stopped the loading of a savegame, which was created after starting a new chat / call and before the first message was displayed.
[*]Fixed wrong cursor scaling behavior.
[*]Fixed a bug where profile updates were skipped.
[*]Fixed a bug which led to blurry outlines for chunk boxes when using ultra wide resolutions.
[*]Fixed a bug where parts of the UI (top and bottom) were outside the game window when using certain aspect ratios.
[*]Fixed a bug which led to big chunk icons at the cursor when using ultra wide screen setups.
[*]Can no longer open the ingame menu while the episode label is still being displayed.
[*]Mac: No longer stretches the UI incorrectly when maximizing the window.
[strike]Win: Is now a x86/64-bit universal application.[/strike][/list]

notes.title: Orwell now available on Mac and Linux!
notes.content:
Hello investigators,

Hope you are all doing well as we lead up to the holiday season. Just a small update today - Orwell is now available for Mac and Linux users.

We have done some limited testing with OS X and Ubuntu, and so far all of our results have been great. That doesn't mean you will not find issues at home; with such a varying landscape of operating systems and hardware configurations, we are expecting some of you to have issues. We have opened up sticky threads for both Mac and Linux - please put any issues you find in there with as much information as possible, and we will aim to help you as quickly as we can.

Hope you enjoy the break, and we will see you all in the new year! 

Steve - Community Manager


[h1]Changelog Version 1.0.6194[/h1]

[b]Technical Fixes[/b]
[list][*]The relationship window now dynamically adjusts size to fit the graph. This should prevent portraits from being placed where they cannot be clicked.
[*]Fixed a bug where the datachunk information window appeared partially outside of the screen, causing the disable / enable button to be unclickable.
[*]Fixed a bug that led to massively increased loading times to enter the main menu after loading savegames and entering main menu repeatedly.
[*]Now uses application icons in different resolutions, fixes grainy taskbar icons.[/list]

notes.content:
Investigators,

We have some great news! Today we are proud to announce that Orwell will be released as a five-part series on a weekly schedule! The first episode "The Clocks were Striking Thirteen" is available right now as a free demo [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/543080]via Steam[/url]!

In this episode, the player is recruited into the Orwell program and, following a terrorist attack, is given their first target to investigate. Cassandra Watergate is a young woman with a criminal record who was spotted by surveillance cameras at the site of the bombing. Digging into her social media, chat messages and online presence, the player starts to uncover a web of connections and a mysterious group who might be involved in the attack.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25928706/b5bbbf8699073257df25520d02e2fb65c053f704.png[/img]

If you enjoy the first episode (and we hope you do), you can [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/491950]pre-order the game directly on Steam[/url] to ensure that you gain access to the next episode as soon as it drops. The best news - your save game from the demo will work with the full version of the game!

[h1]WEEKLY EPISODIC RELEASE SCHEDULE[/h1]

[list] 
[*][b]Oct 20:[/b] Episode One - The Clocks were Striking Thirteen
[*][b]Oct 27:[/b] Episode Two - A Place where there is No Darkness
[*][b]Nov 03:[/b] Episode Three - Unperson
[*][b]Nov 10:[/b] Episode Four - Memory Hole
[*][b]Nov 17:[/b] Episode Five - Under the Spreading Chestnut Tree
[/list]

We've also created [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/491950/discussions/0/333656722966701487/]a small FAQ on the Steam community board[/url] for you.

We hope you enjoy Orwell!

Cheers 
The Osmotic Studios Team
